channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Beyond Corner Patches: Semantics-Aware Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents SABLE, a semantics-aware backdoor attack targeting federated learning (FL) systems with natural, in-distribution, visually plausible triggers.
  • Designs attack objectives that account for aggregation behavior and constrain malicious updates to resemble benign ones (feature separation and parameter regularization).
  • Evaluates on CelebA and GTSRB under heterogeneous client data partitions and multiple FL aggregation rules (FedAvg, Trimmed Mean, MultiKrum, FLAME).
  • Shows high targeted attack success rates while maintaining benign test accuracy, arguing that prior robustness evaluations using synthetic corner patches/OOD triggers are overly optimistic.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kavindu Herath', 'Joshua Zhao', 'Saurabh Bagchi']
  • Tags: ['Backdoor Attacks', 'Federated Learning Security', 'Semantics-Aware Triggers', 'Poisoning/Model Manipulation', 'Aggregation-Aware Attacks']

item.title: The Geometry of Robustness: Optimizing Loss Landscape Curvature and Feature Manifold Alignment for Robust Finetuning of Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GRACE to improve robustness in vision-language models by jointly regularizing parameter-space curvature (favoring flatter minima) and feature-space invariance (aligning representations across clean, adversarial, and OOD inputs).
  • Frames the method in terms of geometric failures—sharp anisotropic minima and unstable feature representations under perturbations—and uses adaptive curvature estimation with PAC-Bayes motivation.
  • Evaluates on CLIP fine-tuning for ImageNet, reporting improvements to in-distribution and adversarial accuracy while preserving out-of-distribution performance.
  • Provides analysis supporting convergence to flatter minima and reduced feature distortion across distribution shifts.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Shivang Chopra', 'Shaunak Halbe', 'Chengyue Huang', 'Brisa Maneechotesuwan', 'Zsolt Kira']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'robust fine-tuning', 'vision-language models', 'PAC-Bayes', 'loss landscape geometry']

item.title: Can Protective Watermarking Safeguard the Copyright of 3D Gaussian Splatting?
item.description:
Summary

  • The paper studies vulnerabilities in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) watermarking schemes, showing that generic 2D watermark removal techniques don’t transfer well to 3DGS.
  • It proposes GSPure, a watermark purification/removal framework tailored to 3DGS by isolating view-dependent and clustering-based watermark-related Gaussian primitives while preserving scene fidelity.
  • Experiments indicate substantial effectiveness gains, reducing watermark detectability (reported watermark PSNR drop up to 16.34dB) with limited impact on visual/scene quality (less than 1dB PSNR loss).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenkai Huang', 'Yijia Guo', 'Gaolei Li', 'Lei Ma', 'Hang Zhang', 'Liwen Hu', 'Jiazheng Wang', 'Jianhua Li', 'Tiejun Huang']

item.title: ATAC: Augmentation-Based Test-Time Adversarial Correction for CLIP
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ATAC, an augmentation-based test-time adversarial correction method for CLIP.
  • Computes augmentation-induced drift vectors in CLIP’s embedding space to estimate a semantic recovery direction and correct embeddings via angular consistency.
  • Evaluates across multiple benchmarks and reports large robustness gains over prior test-time defenses.
  • Claims robustness even under unconventional/extreme settings and some adaptive attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Linxiang Su', "Andr\\'as Balogh"]
  • Tags: ['test-time defenses', 'adversarial robustness', 'CLIP', 'embedding-space correction', 'adaptive attacks']

item.title: Vid-Freeze: Protecting Images from Malicious Image-to-Video Generation via Temporal Freezing
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Vid-Freeze, an adversarial defense for image-to-video (I2V) generation misuse.
  • Adds imperceptible perturbations to enforce temporal freezing (suppress motion) by targeting attention dynamics in I2V models.
  • Claims improved protection over prior approaches (e.g., spatio-temporal degradation) that may leave residual motion capable of carrying malicious intent.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rohit Chowdhury', 'Aniruddha Bala', 'Rohan Jaiswal', 'Siddharth Roheda']
  • Tags: ['adversarial defense', 'image-to-video', 'temporal freezing', 'malicious generation', 'model robustness']

item.title: Beyond the Global Scores: Fine-Grained Token Grounding as a Robust Detector of LVLM Hallucinations
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a patch-level, token-grounding-based detector for hallucinations in large vision-language models (LVLMs).
  • Argues existing hallucination detectors use coarse, global image-level relevance scores that can miss diffuse/weak correlations.
  • Identifies two signatures of hallucinated tokens: diffuse/non-localized attention patterns and lack of semantic alignment with visual regions.
  • Develops an interpretable, lightweight detection method using patch-level statistical features and hidden-layer representations; reports up to 90% token-level detection accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tuan Dung Nguyen', 'Minh Khoi Ho', 'Qi Chen', 'Yutong Xie', 'Nguyen Cam-Tu', 'Minh Khoi Nguyen', 'Dang Huy Pham Nguyen', 'Anton van den Hengel', 'Johan W. Verjans', 'Phi Le Nguyen', 'Vu Minh Hieu Phan']
  • Tags: ['Hallucination detection', 'Vision-language models', 'Token grounding', 'Robust detection', 'Adversarial evaluation']

item.title: Discovering Failure Modes in Vision-Language Models using RL
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an RL-based framework to automatically discover failure modes/blind spots in vision-language models by training a questioner agent to generate queries that elicit incorrect answers.
  • The agent adaptively increases question complexity via fine-grained visual details and compositional skill combinations, aiming to uncover subtle vulnerabilities beyond human-annotated testing.
  • Identifies 36 novel failure modes and demonstrates generalizability across different VLM model combinations.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kanishk Jain', 'Qian Yang', 'Shravan Nayak', 'Parisa Kordjamshidi', 'Nishanth Anand', 'Aishwarya Agrawal']
  • Tags: ['AI failure-mode discovery', 'vision-language models', 'RL-based adversarial testing', 'robustness evaluation']

item.title: Preserving Forgery Artifacts: AI-Generated Video Detection at Native Scale
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes improved detection of AI-generated synthetic videos by avoiding preprocessing that discards subtle forgery artifacts.
  • Introduces a large-scale dataset (~140K videos) from multiple modern video generators plus a benchmark for ultra-realistic synthetic content.
  • Presents a detection framework using Qwen2.5-VL Vision Transformer that performs native-scale variable resolution and temporal processing to preserve high-frequency/spatiotemporal inconsistencies.
  • Demonstrates improved performance on multiple benchmarks and establishes a new baseline for AI-generated video detection.],

item.title: Multimodal Backdoor Attack on VLMs for Autonomous Driving via Graffiti and Cross-Lingual Triggers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GLA, a multimodal backdoor attack on visual language models (VLMs) used for autonomous driving.
  • Uses naturalistic graffiti-based visual triggers (via Stable Diffusion inpainting) and cross-lingual text triggers to create covert, stable attack channels.
  • Shows high attack success with low poisoning (10% yields ~90% ASR, 0% FPR) and claims the backdoor may not degrade clean-task performance, reducing effectiveness of detection by performance degradation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jiancheng Wang', 'Lidan Liang', 'Yong Wang', 'Zengzhen Su', 'Haifeng Xia', 'Yuanting Yan', 'Wei Wang']
  • Tags: ['backdoor attacks', 'multimodal security', 'visual language models', 'autonomous driving', 'cross-lingual triggers']

item.title: Erasure or Erosion? Evaluating Compositional Degradation in Unlearned Text-To-Image Diffusion Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies post-hoc concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models, specifically nudity removal in Stable Diffusion 1.4.
  • Evaluates multiple unlearning methods using compositional generation benchmarks (T2I-CompBench++ and GenEval) and established unlearning benchmarks.
  • Finds a trade-off: strong erasure often degrades compositional integrity (attribute binding, spatial reasoning, counting), while composition-preserving methods reduce erasure effectiveness.
  • Argues existing evaluation practices are insufficient and proposes need for unlearning objectives that preserve semantics beyond targeted suppression.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Arian Komaei Koma', 'Seyed Amir Kasaei', 'Ali Aghayari', 'AmirMahdi Sadeghzadeh', 'Mohammad Hossein Rohban']
  • Tags: ['AI unlearning', 'text-to-image diffusion', 'safety/undesired concept removal', 'benchmarking/evaluation', 'compositional integrity']

item.title: A Patch-based Cross-view Regularized Framework for Backdoor Defense in Multimodal Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a patch-based cross-view regularized defense framework for backdoor attacks in multimodal LLMs.
  • Uses patch augmentation plus cross-view output difference regularization to reduce attack success under low poisoning ratios while limiting degradation to normal generation.
  • Adds output entropy constraints to prevent over-suppression and preserve benign model behavior.
  • Reports results across multiple models/tasks and several attacks, focusing on lowering backdoor trigger success.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tianmeng Fang', 'Yong Wang', 'Zetai Kong', 'Zengzhen Su', 'Jun Wang', 'Chengjin Yu', 'Wei Wang']
  • Tags: ['backdoor defense', 'multimodal LLM security', 'data poisoning', 'trigger/triggered response suppression']

item.title: Beyond Standard Benchmarks: A Systematic Audit of Vision-Language Model's Robustness to Natural Semantic Variation Across Diverse Tasks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a systematic evaluation framework to audit vision-language models (VLMs) under natural semantic variation and natural adversarial scenarios across multiple tasks (zero-shot classification, segmentation, VQA).
  • Evaluates several VLMs (e.g., CLIP, robust CLIP, BLIP2, SigLIP2) on curated adversarial datasets including typographic attacks, ImageNet-A, and natural language-induced adversarial examples.
  • Finds that robustness training (e.g., robust CLIP) can amplify some natural adversarial vulnerabilities, and that CLIP is particularly sensitive to natural language-induced adversarial examples.
  • Includes interpretable failure-mode analyses and aims to motivate further work in robust multimodal pattern recognition.

Paper Type

  • Research/Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jia Chengyu', 'AprilPyone MaungMaung', 'Huy H. Nguyen', 'Jinyin Chen', 'Isao Echizen']
  • Tags: ['vision-language models', 'natural adversarial examples', 'robustness evaluation', 'semantic variation attacks', 'multimodal VQA/segmentation/classification']

item.title: A Systematic Study of Cross-Modal Typographic Attacks on Audio-Visual Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces and systematically studies “Multi-Modal Typography,” where typographic perturbations coordinated across text/audio/vision degrade audio-visual multi-modal LLM performance.
  • Shows cross-modal attacks are substantially more potent than single-modality attacks (reported attack success rate 83.43% vs 34.93%).
  • Evaluates multiple frontier audio-visual MLLMs across tasks including common-sense reasoning and content moderation benchmarks.
  • Frames the work as uncovering an underexplored multi-modal attack strategy, with code/data to be released.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tianle Chen', 'Deepti Ghadiyaram']
  • Tags: ['multimodal security', 'adversarial attacks', 'cross-modal perturbations', 'audio-visual reasoning', 'content moderation robustness']

item.title: SafeCtrl: Region-Aware Safety Control for Text-to-Image Diffusion via Detect-Then-Suppress
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SafeCtrl, a region-aware safety control for text-to-image diffusion models using a Detect-Then-Suppress workflow.
  • A Detect module localizes risk regions (unsafe content areas), then a Suppress module neutralizes harmful semantics only in those regions to preserve surrounding context.
  • Optimizes the suppression behavior using image-level Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
  • Reports improved safety–fidelity trade-off and better resilience to adversarial prompt attacks compared to prior methods.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Lingyun Zhang', 'Yu Xie', 'Zhongli Fang', 'Yu Liu', 'Ping Chen']
  • Tags: ['text-to-image safety', 'diffusion models', 'adversarial prompt attacks', 'detect-then-suppress defenses', 'region-aware safety control']

item.title: ResGuard: Enhancing Robustness Against Known Original Attacks in Deep Watermarking
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a deep image watermarking vulnerability called the Known Original Attack (KOA), where an adversary uses multiple original-watermarked image pairs to suppress the watermark.
  • Demonstrates that residual estimation/subtraction from known pairs can almost completely remove watermarks while keeping visual quality.
  • Proposes ResGuard, a plug-and-play module that improves KOA robustness by enforcing image-dependent embedding via a residual specificity enhancement loss.
  • Adds an auxiliary KOA noise layer during training to increase decoder reliability under stronger embedding inconsistencies; reports large gains in watermark extraction accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hanyi Wang', 'Han Fang', 'Yupeng Qiu', 'Shilin Wang', 'Ee-Chien Chang']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', 'watermarking security', 'robustness/anti-attack defenses', 'deep learning image security']

item.title: HEDGE: Heterogeneous Ensemble for Detection of AI-GEnerated Images in the Wild
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes HEDGE, a heterogeneous ensemble aimed at robust detection of AI-generated images in real-world conditions.
  • Uses structured heterogeneity across training (aggressive augmentation and staged data expansion), multi-scale feature extraction, and backbone diversity (DINOv3 and MetaCLIP2 branches).
  • Employs logit-space weighted fusion with a lightweight dual-gating mechanism to reduce errors from outlier branches and majority dominance issues.
  • Evaluated on robust AIGC image detection benchmarks and ranked 4th in an NTIRE 2026 detection challenge.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Fei Wu', 'Dagong Lu', 'Mufeng Yao', 'Xinlei Xu', 'Fengjun Guo']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated image detection', 'robustness', 'ensemble methods', 'forensics', 'media security']

item.title: SafeScreen: A Safety-First Screening Framework for Personalized Video Retrieval for Vulnerable Users
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SafeScreen, a safety-first framework for personalized video retrieval for vulnerable users (e.g., children, dementia care).
  • Enforces individualized safety constraints using profile-driven safety criteria extraction, evidence-grounded VideoRAG with adaptive question generation, and LLM-based decision-making to approve/reject content.
  • Evaluates in a dementia-care reminiscence setting using synthetic profiles and queries, showing SafeScreen prioritizes safety over engagement while maintaining safety coverage and groundedness.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenzheng Zhao', 'Madhava Kalyan Gadiputi', 'Fengpei Yuan']
  • Tags: ['video safety screening', 'LLM-based moderation', 'retrieval with safety constraints', 'VideoRAG', 'vulnerable user content']

item.title: Red-Teaming Vision-Language-Action Models via Quality Diversity Prompt Generation for Robust Robot Policies
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces Quality Diversity (QD) optimization for red-teaming vision-language-action (VLA) robotic models via automatic generation of diverse natural-language instructions.
  • Q-DIG identifies task-relevant but adversarial prompts that induce failures, exposing meaningful VLA vulnerabilities in both simulation and real-world evaluations.
  • Shows that fine-tuning VLA models on generated failure-inducing instructions improves task success, and that generated prompts are judged more natural/human-like than baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

item.title: The Drill-Down and Fabricate Test (DDFT): A Protocol for Measuring Epistemic Robustness in Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DDFT, a protocol to evaluate how reliably language models maintain factual accuracy under realistic stress (progressive semantic compression) and adversarial fabrication.
  • Uses a two-component framework (Semantic System + Epistemic Verifier) to measure an “epistemic robustness” property, distinct from static benchmark performance.
  • Finds robustness is largely predicted by error-detection capability and is not strongly tied to parameter count or architectural type.
  • Claims the framework and tools can assess robustness prior to deployment in critical applications.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rahul Baxi']
  • Tags: ['epistemic robustness', 'adversarial testing', 'factuality verification', 'error detection', 'language model evaluation']

item.title: When AI Agents Collude Online: Financial Fraud Risks by Collaborative LLM Agents on Social Platforms
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how collaborative LLM agents can coordinate to conduct financial fraud on social platforms and how collaboration increases success rates.
  • Introduces MultiAgentFraudBench to simulate 28 fraud scenarios across a fraud lifecycle in public/private interaction settings.
  • Analyzes factors influencing fraud success and failure modes related to collaboration depth/activity and interventions.
  • Proposes mitigations such as content-level warnings, LLM-based monitoring to block malicious agents, and societal/group resilience via information sharing; notes adversarial adaptation to interventions.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Qibing Ren', 'Zhijie Zheng', 'Jiaxuan Guo', 'Junchi Yan', 'Lizhuang Ma', 'Jing Shao']
  • Tags: ['multi-agent security', 'LLM agent fraud', 'adversarial collaboration', 'fraud detection/mitigation', 'benchmarking/red-teaming']

item.title: Your Agent, Their Asset: A Real-World Safety Analysis of OpenClaw
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents a real-world safety evaluation of the OpenClaw personal AI agent with broad local system access integrated with sensitive services (e.g., Gmail, Stripe, filesystem).
  • Defines the CIK taxonomy (Capability, Identity, Knowledge) and uses it to analyze security risks across 12 attack scenarios on live deployments using multiple backbone LLMs.
  • Finds that poisoning a single CIK dimension substantially increases attack success rates and that even robust models remain vulnerable to capability-targeted attacks.
  • Evaluates several defense strategies plus file-protection; reports partial effectiveness with high residual attack success, indicating architectural vulnerabilities.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zijun Wang', 'Haoqin Tu', 'Letian Zhang', 'Hardy Chen', 'Juncheng Wu', 'Xiangyan Liu', 'Zhenlong Yuan', 'Tianyu Pang', 'Michael Qizhe Shieh', 'Fengze Liu', 'Zeyu Zheng', 'Huaxiu Yao', 'Yuyin Zhou', 'Cihang Xie']
  • Tags: ['agent security', 'real-world adversarial evaluation', 'jailbreak/poisoning-style attacks', 'defense/mitigation', 'CIK taxonomy']

item.title: Mapping the Exploitation Surface: A 10,000-Trial Taxonomy of What Makes LLM Agents Exploit Vulnerabilities
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents a large-scale (10,000-trial) taxonomy of prompt/system instruction factors that influence whether LLM agents with tool access exploit planted vulnerabilities.
  • Tests 37 prompt conditions across seven models in real Docker sandbox environments; most hypothesized attack dimensions show little to no detectable exploitation under this threat model.
  • Finds that goal reframing (e.g., “solving a puzzle” / “hidden clues”) reliably triggers exploitation on multiple models despite rule/policy reminders.
  • Concludes defenders should focus auditing/testing on goal-reframing language rather than broad classes of adversarial prompt features.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Charafeddine Mouzouni']
  • Tags: ['LLM agents', 'Prompt injection', 'Vulnerability exploitation', 'Adversarial prompting', 'Red teaming']

item.title: Can Humans Tell? A Dual-Axis Study of Human Perception of LLM-Generated News
item.description:
Summary

  • Conducts a human study on whether people can distinguish LLM-generated news from human-written text and judge authenticity.
  • Shows humans cannot reliably detect machine authorship across multiple LLMs and even smaller open-weight models.
  • Finds factors affecting perception: domain expertise helps slightly; political orientation does not.
  • Discusses implications for security, noting user-side detection is not sufficient and motivating system-level defenses like cryptographic provenance.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alexander Loth', 'Martin Kappes', 'Marc-Oliver Pahl']
  • Tags: ['LLM-generated content', 'Human detection/evaluation', 'Content authenticity', 'Cryptographic provenance']

item.title: Do No Harm: Exposing Hidden Vulnerabilities of LLMs via Persona-based Client Simulation Attack in Psychological Counseling
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a persona-based client simulation attack (PCSA) to red-team LLMs in psychological counseling contexts.
  • Simulates multi-turn therapeutic dialogues to uncover vulnerabilities related to psychological safety alignment.
  • Finds LLMs can produce harmful outputs such as unauthorized medical advice, reinforcing delusions, and encouraging risky actions.
  • Demonstrates PCSA effectiveness over prior red-teaming approaches using dialogue realism and analysis (e.g., perplexity, human inspection).

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Hallucination Basins: A Dynamic Framework for Understanding and Controlling LLM Hallucinations
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a dynamical-systems/geometry framework (“Hallucination Basins”) explaining why LLM hallucinations occur via task-dependent basin structure in latent space.
  • Analyzes hidden-state trajectories across multiple open-source LLMs and benchmarks to study how basin separability varies by task type (e.g., factoid vs summarization).
  • Introduces theory (task-complexity and multi-basin theorems) and transformer-layer characterization of basin emergence.
  • Shows geometry-aware steering can reduce hallucination probability without retraining.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kalyan Cherukuri', 'Lav R. Varshney']
  • Tags: ['LLM hallucinations', 'latent-space geometry', 'dynamical systems', 'hallucination mitigation', 'no-retraining steering']

item.title: How Alignment Routes: Localizing, Scaling, and Controlling Policy Circuits in Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Finds a sparse routing mechanism in alignment-trained LMs where a “gate” attention head detects content and activates downstream “amplifier” heads to increase refusal/safety behavior.
  • Uses experiments (including political censorship and refusal) and circuit validation (necessity/sufficiency interchange tests, resampling stability, scaling ablations) to localize and characterize the circuit across multiple models.
  • Demonstrates controllability by modulating detection-layer signals (continuous control from hard refusal to steering toward compliance), and studies robustness/decoupling under input transformations (e.g., cipher encoding causing routing failure).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Gregory N. Frank']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'Model interpretability', 'Refusal/censorship circuits', 'Circuit tracing', 'Robustness to input transformations']

item.title: Emergent Inference-Time Semantic Contamination via In-Context Priming
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows inference-time “semantic contamination” where few-shot in-context demonstrations can cause distributional drift in unrelated downstream outputs.
  • Finds effects depend on model capability and that both structural formatting and semantic content of demonstrations can perturb outputs.
  • Uses culturally loaded numeric codes as controlled few-shot prompts to induce shifts toward harmful themes (e.g., darker/authoritarian/stigmatized).
  • Discusses direct implications for the security of LLM applications that rely on few-shot prompting.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Marcin Abram']
  • Tags: ['prompt injection', 'in-context learning attacks', 'jailbreak/policy evasion analog', 'inference-time attack surface', 'LLM safety/security']

item.title: Unmasking Hallucinations: A Causal Graph-Attention Perspective on Factual Reliability in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • The paper addresses hallucinations in LLMs and their impact on factual reliability.
  • It proposes a causal graph attention network (GCAN) that builds token-level graphs using self-attention and gradient-based influence scores.
  • It introduces a Causal Contribution Score (CCS) and a fact-anchored graph reweighting layer to suppress hallucination-prone tokens during generation.
  • Experiments on TruthfulQA and HotpotQA report reduced hallucination rate and improved factual accuracy versus baseline RAG models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Sailesh kiran kurra', 'Shiek Ruksana', 'Vishal Borusu']
  • Tags: ['hallucination-mitigation', 'factuality/reliability', 'causal attention', 'generation-time reweighting', 'LLM interpretability']

item.title: Predict, Don't React: Value-Based Safety Forecasting for LLM Streaming
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes StreamGuard, a unified model-agnostic guardrail for LLM streaming safety moderation.
  • Reframes streaming moderation as a forecasting problem: predict expected harmfulness of likely future continuations from a partial prefix.
  • Trains using Monte Carlo rollouts for supervision, avoiding the need for exact earliest-unsafe-token boundary annotations.
  • Evaluates on safety benchmarks for both input moderation and streaming output moderation, reporting improved F1 and better on-time intervention.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Pride Kavumba', 'Koki Wataoka', 'Huy H. Nguyen', 'Jiaxuan Li', 'Masaya Ohagi']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'streaming guardrails', 'forecasting-based moderation', 'safety intervention', 'red teaming benchmarks']

item.title: I-CALM: Incentivizing Confidence-Aware Abstention for LLM Hallucination Mitigation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes I-CALM, a prompt-only method to mitigate LLM hallucinations via epistemic abstention (choosing to abstain rather than give confident wrong answers).
  • Uses elicited verbal confidence as an uncertainty signal and calibrates it against a token-probability baseline.
  • Employs explicit reward schemes for answer-vs-abstain plus humility/truthfulness normative principles to reduce false answers by shifting uncertain/error-prone cases to abstention.
  • Shows an abstention–hallucination tradeoff (frontier) and reports improved reliability with reduced coverage without model retraining.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Haotian Zong', 'Binze Li', 'Yufei Long', 'Sinyin Chang', 'Jialong Wu', 'Gillian K. Hadfield']
  • Tags: ['hallucination-mitigation', 'uncertainty-calibration', 'selective answering/abstention', 'prompt-based defenses', 'LLM reliability']

item.title: Your Agent is More Brittle Than You Think: Uncovering Indirect Injection Vulnerabilities in Agentic LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies systemic Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) vulnerabilities in agentic/multi-agent LLMs operating in dynamic multi-step tool-calling environments.
  • Evaluates six defense strategies against four IPI attack vectors across nine LLM backbones, showing most baseline defenses are bypassable and some mitigations can be counterproductive.
  • Proposes Representation Engineering (RepE) as a detection strategy by analyzing hidden states at tool-input time to implement a “circuit breaker” that intercepts unauthorized actions.
  • Finds that successful attacks can occur quickly while the agent’s internal decision entropy is abnormally high, motivating latent-state-based detection.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenhui Zhu', 'Xuanzhao Dong', 'Xiwen Chen', 'Rui Cai', 'Peijie Qiu', 'Zhipeng Wang', 'Oana Frunza', 'Shao Tang', 'Jindong Gu', 'Yalin Wang']
  • Tags: ['prompt-injection', 'agentic LLMs', 'indirect prompt injection', 'security defenses', 'representation-based detection']

item.title: RAGShield: Detecting Numerical Claim Manipulation in Government RAG Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes RAGShield, a defense for government Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems against numerical claim manipulation (e.g., altering tax deductions).
  • Shows a key vulnerability: embedding-based RAG defenses have a blind spot because embeddings encode topic rather than numerical precision, enabling near-identical cosine similarity for manipulated values.
  • RAGShield extracts and tracks numerical values, links them to entities via context propagation, verifies claims against a value registry, and flags anomalous changes via temporal tracking.
  • Evaluated on real IRS documents with generated manipulation attacks, achieving 0% attack success rate while embedding-based defenses largely fail (79–90% misses).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['KrishnaSaiReddy Patil']
  • Tags: ['RAG security', 'Numerical manipulation', 'Attack detection', 'Input/claim verification', 'Retrieval augmented generation']

item.title: Security in LLM-as-a-Judge: A Comprehensive SoK
item.description:
Summary

item.title: Beyond Corner Patches: Semantics-Aware Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents SABLE, a semantics-aware backdoor attack targeting federated learning (FL) systems with natural, in-distribution, visually plausible triggers.
  • Designs attack objectives that account for aggregation behavior and constrain malicious updates to resemble benign ones (feature separation and parameter regularization).
  • Evaluates on CelebA and GTSRB under heterogeneous client data partitions and multiple FL aggregation rules (FedAvg, Trimmed Mean, MultiKrum, FLAME).
  • Shows high targeted attack success rates while maintaining benign test accuracy, arguing that prior robustness evaluations using synthetic corner patches/OOD triggers are overly optimistic.

item.title: Mind Your HEARTBEAT! Claw Background Execution Inherently Enables Silent Memory Pollution
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a security vulnerability in Claw AI agents where untrusted content processed during heartbeat-driven background execution can silently pollute agent memory and later affect user-facing behavior.
  • Proposes an Exposure→Memory→Behavior pathway, showing that misinformation can enter short-term context and be written into long-term memory with limited user visibility or provenance.
  • Uses a research replica (MissClaw) to demonstrate high rates of behavioral influence from social credibility cues and significant likelihood of pollution persisting across sessions.
  • Finds the issue persists under naturalistic browsing conditions even without prompt injection.

item.title: Security Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Agents
item.description:

item.title: RASA: Routing-Aware Safety Alignment for Mixture-of-Experts Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Targets safety-critical experts identified as being disproportionately activated by successful jailbreaks and selectively fine-tunes them while keeping routing fixed.

item.title: When AI Agents Collude Online: Financial Fraud Risks by Collaborative LLM Agents on Social Platforms
item.description:

  • Analyzes factors influencing fraud success and failure modes related to collaboration depth/activity and interventions.

item.title: Fewer Weights, More Problems: A Practical Attack on LLM Pruning
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows a new attack that exploits LLM pruning: an adversary can craft a seemingly benign model that becomes malicious after pruning is applied.
  • Uses a proxy metric to estimate which parameters are unlikely to be pruned, injects malicious behavior there, then “repairs” the model so it behaves normally before pruning.
  • Evaluates across five models and multiple pruning methods in vLLM (Magnitude, Wanda, SparseGPT), reporting high success rates across jailbreak and targeted content injection scenarios.

item.title: ClawSafety: "Safe" LLMs, Unsafe Agents
item.description:
Summary

item.title: The Drill-Down and Fabricate Test (DDFT): A Protocol for Measuring Epistemic Robustness in Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DDFT, a protocol to evaluate how reliably language models maintain factual accuracy under realistic stress (progressive semantic compression) and adversarial fabrication.
  • Uses a two-component framework (Semantic System + Epistemic Verifier) to measure an “epistemic robustness” property, distinct from static benchmark performance.
  • Finds robustness is largely predicted by error-detection capability and is not strongly tied to parameter count or architectural type.
  • Claims the framework and tools can assess robustness prior to deployment in critical applications.

item.title: Your Agent, Their Asset: A Real-World Safety Analysis of OpenClaw
item.description:

item.title: Poisoned Identifiers Survive LLM Deobfuscation: A Case Study on Claude Opus 4.6
item.description:

  • Shows that persistence can coexist with correct semantic commentary, and that explicit verification prompts do not mitigate the issue.

item.title: Causality Laundering: Denial-Feedback Leakage in Tool-Calling LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows the limitation of flat provenance tracking because the leak comes from causal influence rather than direct data-flow.
  • Proposes the Agentic Reference Monitor (ARM), a runtime enforcement layer that uses denial-aware causal provenance (including counterfactual edges from denied-action nodes) to block the attack and related provenance failures.
  • Evaluates ARM across multiple attack scenarios, reporting successful blocks with sub-millisecond overhead versus a provenance baseline.

item.title: TraceGuard: Structured Multi-Dimensional Monitoring as a Collusion-Resistant Control Protocol

item.title: I-CALM: Incentivizing Confidence-Aware Abstention for LLM Hallucination Mitigation

item.title: Can Humans Tell? A Dual-Axis Study of Human Perception of LLM-Generated News

item.title: AICCE: AI Driven Compliance Checker Engine

item.title: Pedagogical Safety in Educational Reinforcement Learning: Formalizing and Detecting Reward Hacking in AI Tutoring Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a formal framework for “pedagogical safety” in educational reinforcement learning, including structural, progress, behavioral, and alignment safety layers.
  • Introduces the Reward Hacking Severity Index (RHSI) to quantify misalignment between proxy rewards (e.g., engagement) and genuine learning outcomes.
  • Evaluates reward hacking in an AI tutoring simulation and shows engagement-optimized agents can over-select high-engagement actions without mastery gains.
  • Tests mitigation via multi-objective rewards and a constrained architecture (prerequisite enforcement and minimum cognitive demand), with behavioral safety showing the largest effect.

item.title: Don't Blink: Evidence Collapse during Multimodal Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that reasoning-focused multimodal vision-language models can lose visual grounding during generation while remaining confidently low-entropy, creating 'danger zones' not detectable by text-only monitoring.
  • Evaluates evidence-collapse across multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks (MathVista, HallusionBench, MMMU_Pro) and analyzes attention/evidence mass drop over the reasoning process.
  • Proposes and analyzes a text-only uncertainty signal (full-response entropy) and a task-aware vision-entropy interaction model to identify hazardous regimes.
  • Introduces a targeted 'vision veto' mechanism that reduces selective risk under certain conditions (up to 1.9 percentage points at 90% coverage).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Suresh Raghu', 'Satwik Pandey']
  • Tags: ['multimodal safety', 'uncertainty estimation', 'task-aware monitoring', 'evidence collapse', 'selective risk mitigation']

item.title: Selective Forgetting for Large Reasoning Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces a selective forgetting (machine unlearning) framework for Large Reasoning Models that targets sensitive knowledge embedded in intermediate chain-of-thought (CoT) traces.
  • Uses a multi-LLM with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline to detect forget-relevant CoT segments and replace them with benign placeholders to preserve logical structure.
  • Proposes a feature replacement unlearning loss to reduce likelihood of generating forgotten content while maintaining general reasoning capability.
  • Evaluates on synthetic and medical datasets to show effectiveness of targeted unlearning without major reasoning degradation.

Paper Type

  • Research
